headline: Nvidia beats and rises ~3% after hours; S&P 500 falls 1% onto its 200-day line; Taiwan watches 40,000
summary: Nvidia's report gives chip stocks a reason to steady, but US stocks are still in a pullback: the S&P 500 fell 1% to just below its 200-day line, still a pullback in an uptrend by the rules. Taiwan opens against a 3.7% drop in the TSMC ADR, cushioned by Nvidia's after-hours gain; with futures settling today, whether foreign selling keeps easing is key. Keep regular investments on plan.

overview.lead: This was broad selling, not a chip-only rout: every sector fell, while the chip index rose slightly.
points: The S&P 500 fell 1% to 7,340, just below its 200-day line.
The Dow lost 849 points, or 1.6%, the worst of the major indexes.
The software ETF (IGV) fell 3.3%, the hardest-hit group.
The chip index rose 0.3% and Nvidia (NVDA) closed down only 0.4% ahead of earnings.
Equal-weight RSP fell 1.5%, more than SPY, so selling spread beyond big tech.

focus.lead: Among the nine tracked names, pressure sits in the two Taiwan funds: NAVs updated to 11/17 are both more than 30% below their peaks; the two US ETFs are still early in the framework.
points: Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV fell 6.3% on 11/17, now −33.9% from peak, the deepest of the nine.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) NAV fell 4.8% on 11/17, now −30.9% from peak.
The two share 6 top-ten holdings, about 27% by weight: the same AI supply-chain exposure.
QQQ is only 1.7% from tier 3, the closest of the nine to its next tier.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) and both AB funds have NAVs only to 11/16, before the 11/17 drop.
SPY sits on its 200-day line, less than 0.1% away.

position.lead: No new tier was hit today; the closest is QQQ tier 3, only 1.7% away.
points: QQQ tier 3 is 645.71, 1.7% away.
SPY tier 2 is 701.18, 4.3% away.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) tier 5 is 1,218.74, 7.5% away (11/16 NAV).
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 12.2% from tier 5; Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan is 16.1% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used all tiers; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: Rates and the economy are fine; the pressure on US stocks comes from AI valuations, not macro.
points: October retail sales rose 0.2% month on month, slightly above forecasts.
Sales excluding autos and gas rose 0.5%; consumers are holding up.
The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10%, down 0.02 points.
The high-yield spread is 3.34% (11/16), far from the 5% warning line.
USD/TWD is 32.876 (11/16); the dollar is up about 0.49 over a month.

sentiment.lead: Fear is rising but not yet at a bottoming extreme: the VIX jumped above 25, and short-term volatility is above longer-term.
points: The VIX closed at 25.46, up 2.55 points in a day.
Short-term volatility is above the three-month level; the inverted term structure is the only US capitulation signal on.
CNN Fear & Greed is 25, in fear; it was 37 a week ago.
Taiwan margin debt is down 21% over 20 days; deleveraging continues.

sectors.lead: Every US sector fell; software fell hardest while semiconductors held up.
points: The software ETF (IGV) fell 3.3% and is down nearly 10% over a month.
Chip ETF SMH fell only 0.4%; the chip index rose 0.3%.
Financials (XLF) fell 1.9% and utilities (XLU) 1.6%; defensives did not escape.
Optical stocks gave back gains on reports of new US curbs on Chinese data center equipment.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan opens against the TSMC ADR's drop, but Nvidia's after-hours gain should cushion it; whether foreign selling keeps easing is key.
points: The TSMC ADR (TSM) fell 3.7%, about a 9% premium to the Taiwan shares.
The chip index rose 0.3% and Nvidia rose about 3% after hours; chip sentiment is better than at the close.
Foreigners sold a net NT$38.1B on 11/17, nearly half the prior day.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures stand at 97,896 contracts; the November contract settles today.
The NT dollar broke past 33 per USD intraday on 11/17; currency pressure remains.

watch.lead: Three things over the next two days: TAIEX futures settlement today, FOMC minutes early 11/19, and the Anthropic listing on 11/19.
points: November TAIEX futures settle on 11/18; settlement days can be volatile.
FOMC October minutes come out early 11/19 Taipei time.
QQQ tier 3 is 645.71, only 1.7% away.
The TAIEX bear line is 39,858, only 0.6% below the 11/17 close.
US markets close 11/26 for Thanksgiving.

regime.lead: By the rules, both US and Taiwan stocks are still pullbacks in uptrends, not bear turns; but Taiwan now has 2 risk lights on, leaning 'pullback, but risk rising'.
points: Trend: the S&P 500 just slipped under its still-rising 200-day line, by 0.05%, for 1 day.
The TAIEX has closed below its 200-day line for 2 days, 3.2% under; the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: only 'S&P 500 below its 200-day line' is on (1 light); credit, the economy and financial conditions show no stress.
The closest to turning on is the high-yield spread at 3.34%, still far from 5%.
Capitulation signals: 1 on in the US (inverted volatility curve), 3 in Taiwan (margin deleveraging, breadth washout, surge in new lows).
History: US drops to this level are mostly ordinary pullbacks; only 19 of 208 went past −20%.
All 10 Taiwan drops to this level went past −20%; only 3 were this fast, too few to rely on.
What flips the view: 5 S&P 500 closes below 7,345 with a flat line means weak.
A Taiwan close below 39,858 is a bear market by definition; 3 lights on means it may be turning bearish.

news.title: Nvidia (NVDA) Q3 revenue of $115.8B, up 103% year on year; Q4 guidance about $130B, above expectations
news.read: Revenue and guidance beat, giving chips and Taiwan's AI suppliers a reason to steady; guidance excludes China data center revenue, and the 71%–72% gross margin outlook is worth watching.

news.title: Nvidia beats; shares up as much as 4% after hours; Vera Rubin revenue up nearly $20B from last quarter
news.read: The after-hours gain narrowed from 4% to about 3%: buyers, but not euphoria; QQQ and AB International Technology (LU0060230025) benefit most directly.

news.title: US stocks fall: Dow down 848.75 points, S&P 500 down 1.03% to 7,340.53, Nasdaq falls for a fourth day
news.read: The S&P 500 slipped just below its 200-day line, turning on the site's 'US market below 200-day line' risk light; the rules need 5 closes and a flat line to call it weak.

news.title: Software stocks slump: Salesforce down about 8% intraday, ServiceNow about 6%, software ETF nearly 3%
news.read: Selling moved from chips to software as doubts about AI's impact on software models grow; Microsoft (MSFT), a top-three holding of AB International Technology, is in this group.

news.title: US October retail sales rose 0.2%, slightly above forecasts; September revised up to 0.8%; ex autos and gas up 0.5%
news.read: Consumers are not weakening and recession signals are far off; the 10-year yield eased to 5.10%.

news.title: TSMC ADR (TSM) falls 3.68% to $359.69 as chip stocks turn cautious before Nvidia's report
news.read: The ADR drop is Taiwan's first hurdle at today's open; TSMC is the largest weight in 0050 and both Taiwan funds; Nvidia's after-hours gain may offset part of it.

news.title: Nvidia's board says it does not plan to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and an outside search is under way
news.read: With earnings cleared, leadership uncertainty is Nvidia's remaining wildcard; Huang will sit for a closed-door House committee interview on 12/1.

news.title: Institutions sell a net NT$54.7B: foreigners NT$38.1B, trusts NT$0.9B
news.read: Foreign selling was nearly half the prior day; today shows whether it keeps easing or grows again with the ADR drop.
